description: Converts the spherical coordinates r, theta and phi into the cartesian coordinates X, Y and Z; at audio rates the effect resembles ring modulation

params.text: Chooses the radius scaling: at 1 to 1 a +/-5V radius keeps X, Y and Z inside +/-5V; at the square root of three to one it reaches every point in that cube, with some outputs passing +/-5V
Sets oversampling to off, x2 or x4 against aliasing from the conversion; each step costs considerable CPU, so the lowest one that gives the sound wanted is the one to use

inputs.text: The radial distance r, with negative values accepted
The polar angle theta at 36 degrees per volt, so 5V is 180 degrees; any angle is accepted
The azimuthal angle phi at 36 degrees per volt, so 5V is 180 degrees; any angle is accepted

outputs.text: The x coordinate: r times the sine of theta times the cosine of phi
The y coordinate: r times the sine of theta times the sine of phi
The z coordinate: r times the cosine of theta

menu: Oversample filter quality — 10th order by default, with 8th order and a cheaper 6th order; 10th and 8th cut at 80% of Nyquist and 6th at 50%
